text:
Michael Eyssimont made his season debut on Nov. 8 and scored against Florida, and Sports Illustrated had him on a new-look second line with Morgan Geekie that week. Boston hasn't won since. Across the three losses that followed, he's played about ten minutes a night and put six shots on goal without scoring.

Four games is a tiny sample, so read everything here loosely. He's shooting plenty (nine shots, a high rate of chances for his minutes), and the Bruins have outshot opponents with him on the ice at five on five. The quality has gone the other way: Boston has only 44.5% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, in those minutes.

That fits who he's been. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 61% of his shots coming off the rush last season, and noted his value doesn't come from creating five-on-five offense. Evolving-Hockey had his small positive value coming on defense, against tough competition (92nd percentile). The Colorado native is on his fifth NHL team; his job is to make life hard, not to carry a line.
